scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from July to September
problem_definition_history.root_problem: A change to billing import validation rules in August caused systematic mis-billing of actual meter reads, leading to a doubling of dispute tickets.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-10: While actual reads still exceed estimated reads among disputed bills, E-10 shows many disputed estimated bills stem from AMI reads rejected due to high consumption, indicating estimation errors may underlie the surge.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-AMI-READ-GAP.statement: AMI read deliveries degraded or were missing in August-September, leading to estimation errors and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Field manual read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) failed or was delayed, causing missing reads and estimation‑based billing errors.

H-BILL-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) introduced in August caused systematic mis‑billing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows that disputed bills are more often associated with actual meter reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that the dispute surge is not primarily driven by estimation errors.

While actual reads still exceed estimated reads among disputed bills, E-10 shows many disputed estimated bills stem from AMI reads rejected due to high consumption, indicating estimation errors may underlie the surge.
The observation shows dispute tickets rose from 590 in July to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, marking a roughly two‑fold increase starting in August.
The dispute volume increase remains, but E-10 provides an alternative cause: high consumption causing AMI read rejections, which fall back to estimation and generate disputed bills.
The tariff change log shows no tariff changes were recorded, indicating that tariff modifications did not occur during the period.

The route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that field manual read collection fell short of expectations, which could contribute to missing reads and estimation‑based billing issues.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The shortage of three field readers since July has caused routes to run late, resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.
The observation shows that dispute tickets are being answered within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days) with a total of 2,440 tickets in the period.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states that there has been no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a factor in the recent dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes require Field Operations Manager confirmation, aligning with the existing K-DISPATCH constraint.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation indicates that MDMS export access is now available, enabling verification of AMI read delivery data for August‑September, which is relevant to assessing whether missing AMI reads contributed to the dispute surge.
Among disputed estimated bills, most have AMI reads that were delivered before cutoff but rejected due to high consumption, while a small fraction had no AMI read received.
